rows.purpose: Bumped whenever a message layout changes.
First port the host tries to listen on.
Consecutive ports tried when one is taken.
Pose messages per second.
How far behind the newest pose the double is shown, so motion is smooth.
Silence after which the peer is dropped.
How long a joiner keeps trying before it reports failure.
Frames the local hero must exist before a double is spawned.
Caught faults after which the mod turns itself off for the session.
Jump between poses that is shown as a snap, not a glide.
Most suit part ids carried in one suit message.
How often the double's mask and hood are applied again while its suit is still loading.
How long after a spawn the mask and hood keep being applied again.
How often the mod writes its per-frame cost to its log.
Map element type given to the other player's double: the game's person marker (pink square with a silhouette).
Number of lighting modes; an index outside 0 to this minus 1 is ignored.
Least time between two requests to match the host's lighting mode, so a game that keeps changing it back is not flooded.
Most enemies the host shares at once; the nearest are kept.
The host shares an enemy within this distance of either player.
How often the host walks the object table for enemies.
Pose updates per second for each shared enemy.
A puppet whose enemy has not been heard from for this long is removed.
How far behind the newest enemy pose a puppet is shown; longer than the player's because enemies are sent less often.
Rig slots read on an animation controller; the largest joint count among them is the rig's.
After asking the game to load an enemy's actor, wait this long before spawning puppets of it, so they are not built from a half-loaded actor.
Items in the game's own pause list; the mod adds its items only when it finds exactly this many.
Id of the added Go to your friend item (above the game's own ids, so the game ignores it).
Id of the added Start a crime (test) item.
How far to the side of the other player Go to your friend puts you.
If you are this far from the warp target a second later (a perch pulled you back), warp again, once.

A shared enemy that still exists but drops out of the host's scan (out of range, not animating) keeps being shared for this many scans, so a one-second hiccup does not remove and respawn it on the joiner.
How often the joiner logs a summary of the enemy copies it shows (how many, how far from you, how many waiting to load).
While joined to a host, the joiner's random crime countdown is held at least this high, so its own game starts no crimes; the host's crimes are the shared ones.
